name: Pet Health Checklist
description: A complete checklist to help pet owners keep a dog or cat healthy with routine care, prevention, and early warning signs.

items.text: Schedule a yearly wellness exam for healthy adult pets
Book more frequent visits for puppies, kittens, and seniors
Keep a record of each visit, diagnosis, and advice
Bring your questions and a list of any changes you noticed
Confirm when the next check-up or test is due
items.note: Ask your vet how often your pet should be seen

items.text: Keep core vaccines up to date per your vet's plan
Ask about lifestyle vaccines based on risk and region
Stay current on flea and tick prevention
Keep heartworm and intestinal worm prevention on schedule
Store proof of vaccination for boarding and travel
items.note: Vaccine schedules vary by region and vet, so follow your vet's recommendations

items.text: Feed a balanced diet suited to age and size
Provide fresh water and clean bowls daily
Give regular exercise and play for body and mind
Brush teeth and check the mouth for problems
Groom, check skin and coat, and trim nails as needed
Weigh your pet regularly and log the numbers
Feel for ribs and check the waistline for body condition
Measure meals instead of free-feeding when advised
Limit treats to a small share of daily calories
Discuss any quick weight gain or loss with your vet
Changes in appetite, thirst, or weight
Vomiting, diarrhea, or trouble going to the bathroom
Coughing, sneezing, or labored breathing
Low energy, hiding, limping, or stiffness
New lumps, sores, bad breath, or itchy skin
items.note: Contact your vet if signs are severe or do not improve

items.text: Keep an up-to-date file of vaccines and medications
Note your pet's normal weight, diet, and habits
Save your vet's number and the nearest emergency hospital
Confirm microchip details are registered and current
Review pet insurance or savings for unexpected care
This checklist is general information for owners, not veterinary advice; your pet's needs depend on its age, breed, and health, so always consult a licensed veterinarian
items.note: For any emergency, contact your vet or an emergency animal hospital immediately

faq.q: How often should my pet see a vet?
faq.a: Many healthy adult pets benefit from a wellness exam once a year, while puppies, kittens, and seniors often need more frequent visits. Ask your veterinarian what schedule fits your pet's age and health.

faq.q: What are common signs my pet may be sick?
faq.a: Watch for changes in appetite, energy, weight, drinking, or bathroom habits, along with vomiting, coughing, limping, or new lumps. If something seems off or persists, contact your veterinarian.

faq.q: Why does dental care matter for pets?
faq.a: Dental disease is very common and can be painful and affect overall health. Regular tooth brushing at home and professional dental checks help keep your pet's mouth comfortable and clean.

faq.q: Do indoor pets still need parasite prevention?
faq.a: Often yes. Fleas, ticks, and worms can still reach indoor pets, and risk depends on your region and lifestyle. Ask your veterinarian which prevention plan is right for your pet.

faq.q: Is this pet health checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, fill it in for your pet, and use it to track vet visits, vaccines, prevention, and any symptoms you notice over time.
